title: Adaptive timeout tiers, regional downgrade & cached local-rerank fallback for reranker
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: Our reranker endpoint has shown a growing number of customer-facing tail latency incidents under load and during regional outages. Current mitigation relies on naive timeouts and full-service fallbacks which either lose quality or add significant cost.

Goal: Reduce 99th/99.9th percentile inference latency and number of customer-visible failures by 60% during degraded conditions while preserving >=95% of rerank quality for typical traffic. Provide deterministic, auditable downgrade behavior (no silent quality cliffs) and a clear migration path to per-customer policies.

Success metrics (SLOs):
- 99th percentile latency for rerank requests: <= 250ms under nominal load
- 99.9th percentile latency: reduce by 60% during regional contention windows
- Customer-visible timeouts/failures: -75% from baseline during rolling infra incidents
- Quality regression vs full reranker: median NDCG drop <= 5% for routed fallbacks

Proposed design (high level):
1) Adaptive timeout tiers: classify incoming rerank requests into latency budgets (fast, balanced, high-quality) based on client header, route, and historical trace. Use progressive timeout values and early-abort hooks inside the serving runtime to free queue slots.
2) Per-customer circuit breakers: maintain rolling error/latency windows per customer and per-region. Open circuit early for customers exceeding configured thresholds and route to a downgrade path rather than outright failing.
3) Regional soft-downgrade policy: when regional capacity or kernels degrade, automatically route a percentage of traffic to a cheaper model variant (quantized or shorter context) and escalate to cached local ranking for the remainder. Tunable policy: e.g., 20% to variant, 80% to local fallback.
4) Cached local-rerank fallback: serve a lightweight deterministic reranker inside the API node that operates on cached embeddings + a small in-memory ranker (approximate dot-product with heuristic rescoring). This preserves relative ordering in >90% common cases and responds in <30ms. Fall back algorithm must be auditable and testable against stored eval prompts.
5) Queue admission & backpressure: introduce priority queue slots (fast vs standard) with admission control to prevent head-of-line blocking; integrate with autoscaler signals to temporarily expand fast slots for high SLO traffic.
6) Observability and automated rollback: surface per-request decision (path taken, timeout tier, reason for downgrade) to console and tracing. Define automatic rollback thresholds if quality metrics exceed degradation budget.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Local fallback reduces latency but may slightly reduce ranking accuracy; we will gate by quality budgets and customer opt-outs.
- Adding per-customer circuit breakers increases state complexity and data retention needs; we will limit window size and TTL to reduce memory.
- Regional routing adds cross-region egress cost for reroutes; policy favors intra-region fallback first.

Migration & rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (canary): implement adaptive timeouts and early-abort hook in runtime, enable for internal traffic only. (est. 1 sprint)
- Phase 1: deploy cached local-rerank fallback behind a feature flag; enable for 10% of production traffic in region-us-west1 with shadow evaluation to measure NDCG. (est. 1 sprint)
- Phase 2: enable per-customer circuit breakers for top 10 customers and expose UI controls in Console. (est. 1 sprint)
- Phase 3: enable regional soft-downgrade policy with automatic ramping and rollback thresholds; monitor and expand globally. (est. 2 sprints)

Open questions / decisions required:
- Quality baseline for fallback: should we require >=92% relative NDCG on customers' eval sets before enabling? (PM/SE decision)
- Opt-in vs opt-out: default to opt-in for enterprise customers due to audit needs? (legal/compliance input)
- Limits on per-customer circuit breaker state size and retention period.

Acceptance criteria (pre-release):
- Integration tests cover early-abort and queue admission behavior under synthetic load.
- Shadow eval demonstrates median NDCG loss <= 5% and tail latency improvements per plan.
- Dashboard panels created: per-region rerank path breakdown, per-customer circuit breaker status, fallback quality metrics.

Artifacts and links: see links field for design doc, dashboard links, and PRs.
